### 1 — Scene
A mixed meal of scrambled eggs, seasoned rice, roasted potatoes, broccoli, and fruit. A few pale pieces in the rice appear to be chicken, though identification is uncertain.

### 2 — Vessel
A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Using a 26 cm circular approximation:
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm².**

### 3 — Items
Scrambled eggs, seasoned rice, roasted potato chunks, cooked broccoli, strawberries, pineapple, blueberries, and apparent chicken pieces. No distinct pool of sauce or separately measurable oil is visible; cooking fat is included in the prepared-food energy estimates.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
Areas represent non-overlapping visible portions. Bulk density is applied only once.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density (g/ml) | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |

### 8 — Sanity check
The areas sum to **86% coverage**, consistent with this fairly full plate. The estimated **656 g and 726 kcal** are plausible for the visible piles. Plate size, pile depth, and cooking fat introduce substantial uncertainty; a practical range is roughly **550–780 g and 600–900 kcal**.
